--- title: 'Investigating Sociological & Marginalised Themes in Jokes' subtitle: | INFO 523 - Summer 2025 - Final Project
Content warning: this project explores sociopolitical themes in humor data; many jokes contain problematic, vulgar, or taboo language.
author: '(Ahn) Michael Howell & Cat Xia | Repo Link' title-slide-attributes: data-background-size: stretch data-background-opacity: "0.7" data-slide-number: none format: revealjs: theme: ['data/customtheming.scss'] resources: - audio/** editor: visual jupyter: python3 execute: echo: false --- ## Our Dataset [A dataset of English plaintext jokes](https://github.com/taivop/joke-dataset) - ~200k jokes from Reddit - Gathered in 2017 by Taivo Pungas - Had columns: id, title, body, score - Why we chose it: - Very complete data (few missing values) - Text data with sociological topic ## Our Questions 1. What are the distributions of social categories and marginalised themes represented in jokes? 2. How does each sociological theme relate to the scores users assign - are certain themes rated more highly? - Can we create a model to predict how well a joke does, through sociological theme alone? ## Our Approach Identifying sociological themes - 8 themes: gender, ethnicity, sexuality, ability, age, weight, appearance, class - Predefined sets of words to match each theme Key files - [preprocessing_data.ipynb](https://github.com/INFO-523-SU25/final-project-howell-xia/blob/main/preprocess_data.ipynb) - For data preparation & feature engineering - [final_analysis_writeup.ipynb](https://github.com/INFO-523-SU25/final-project-howell-xia/blob/main/final_analysis_writeup.ipynb) - For analysis & presenting findings ## Our Data Prep (NLP) Preprocessing steps - Combining joke title & body (whole_text) - Lowercasing - Removing non-letter characters - Removing stop words Engineering features - whole_text, whole_text_normalised_tokens - distinct_words, overall_length - theme__count, theme__bool, themes_found ## Example Jokes ![](images/ahn/examples/example-jokes.png) ## Plot 1 - Theme prevalence (Bar) ::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} ![](images/ahn/1-bar_plot_theme_prevalence_default.png) ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ![](images/ahn/1-bar_plot_theme_prevalence_strict.png) ::: ::: - Most common: gender, ethnicity & sexuality - Least common: weight, ability - Default: 28% of jokes have no visible social theme - Strict: 63% of jokes have only 1 or no theme words ## Plot 2 - Scores by theme (Box) ![](images/ahn/2-box_plot_scores_default.png){width=60%} - Themeless jokes score much lower (median: 6 upvotes) - Uncommon themes (appearance, age, class) get highest scores - Jokes with ethnic-themed words get lower scores, despite being common - Social progress or jokes becoming covert/subtle? ![](images/ahn/examples/ethnicity-leroy-paint.png) ## Plot 3 - Scores by # of themes (Box) ![](images/ahn/3-box_plot_score_vs_num_themes_default.png) - Clear positive trend: more themes = higher score - There is a falloff point - joke too long, hard to follow ## Plot 4 - Scores by joke length, by theme (Scatter) ![](images/ahn/4-scatter_plot_length_vs_score_default.png){width=60%} - Longer jokes receive lower scores - Jokes with no social theme tend to be shorter - Otherwise no clear trend separating themes here ## Classification ![](images/cat/Classification confusion matrix.png) ## Results | Model | Log Reg | KNN | Decision Tree | Rand Forest | |------------|----------|-------|---------------|-------------| | Accuracy | 57% | 55% | 57% | 57% | | Precision | 58% | 54% | 58% | 58% | | Recall | 30% | 26% | 29% | 29% | | F1 Score | 40% | 35% | 39% | 39% | | ROC AUC | 57% | 55% | 57% | 57% | ## Summary & Next Steps Q1: What are the distributions of themes represented in jokes? - Most jokes involve a social theme, especially gender, ethnicity & sexuality Q2: How does each theme relate to the scores users assign? - Reddit users favor jokes with more social themes - Social theme themselves are not enough to predict how well a joke does **Next steps** - Use an LLM for nuanced theme recognition ## Layouts You can use plain text ::: columns ::: {.column width="40%"} - or bullet points[^1] ::: ::: {.column width="60%"} or in two columns ::: :::
